name: Face Bouquet: Make a Flower Bouquet of Me From Your Selfies
blurb: The face bouquet trend, also called the flower bouquet of me, is a picture of a kraft paper bouquet where every flower is your own face, with different smiles and angles, on pink.

prompts.text: Use the uploaded image as the base. A bouquet in brown kraft paper with a white ribbon on a pink background. Every flower is the face of the person in the photo, with different smiles and angles. The flowers are 7 to 9 cut-out head-and-shoulders portraits of the person in the photo, packed tightly in three rows that rise above the rim of the paper like a round bouquet, each one cut out cleanly along the hair and the shoulders like a sticker, with no white border and no photo background behind it. The front row is the biggest and overlaps the rim a little; the heads behind peek out above and between them. Every head is the same person, with their own hair and the top of their own clothes from the photo. They differ only the way different selfies of one person do: some look straight into the camera, some are turned three-quarters, some tilt the head a little to the left or the right; about half keep the exact expression from the photo, the others show a soft closed-mouth smile or a big happy smile. Make it look like the viral bouquet of me edit: a clean digital sticker collage, not a painting. The bouquet stands upright in the center of the frame, whole from the top heads to the bottom of the wrap, and fills about two thirds of the height. The wrap is a cone of plain matte brown kraft paper, folded in soft overlapping layers, wide and open at the top and narrow at the bottom, tied at the narrow end with a white satin ribbon in a neat bow with small black polka dots. A few small green leaf tips peek out between the heads at the rim of the paper. The background is a smooth, soft pink gradient, lighter in the middle, with no objects and no floor, and a faint soft shadow under the bouquet. Every face is sharp, well lit and large enough to recognize at once, turned to the camera or three-quarters to it, with the eyes open. Photo realistic faces and hair, like real phone selfies cut out and stacked; the paper and the ribbon look real too. Vertical 9:16. No real flowers in place of a face, no extra people, no text, no letters, no numbers, no logo, no watermark, no frame and no border.
